title: The AI Brief — Vol. 02, Issue 28
summary: Fable 5 is restored worldwide on July 1 after a 19-day US export-control suspension, with Anthropic simultaneously launching Claude Sonnet 5 as the new default model for all users; GPT-5.6 Sol deploys on Cerebras at 750 tokens per second — the fastest frontier inference in production. Microsoft commits $2.5B and 6,000 specialists to a new Frontier Company enterprise AI unit, Grok 4.5 enters private beta at SpaceX and Tesla on xAI's 1.5T V9 model, and the Five Eyes alliance warns AI-capable cyberattack models are months away from broad availability.

title: The AI Brief — Vol. 02, Issue 27
summary: OpenAI previews GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna under US government-gated access — Sol Ultra scores 91.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and becomes the first model to cross 50% on Agent's Last Exam — while Mythos 5 is partially restored for ~100 US critical infrastructure operators and Fable 5 remains banned. SpaceX acquires Cursor maker Anysphere for $60B (the largest VC-backed acquisition in history), OpenAI and Broadcom launch the Jalapeño custom inference chip, and enterprise CFOs mandate model-routing strategies cutting per-token costs 70–90%.

title: The AI Brief — Vol. 02, Issue 26
summary: Fable 5 remains offline on Day 11 as autonomous exploit generation — not a jailbreak — is confirmed as the export-control trigger; Altman, Amodei, and Hassabis become the first frontier AI CEOs to jointly address G7 leaders in France, proposing a US-led AI governance forum and chip-trade rules excluding China. Odyssey closes a $310M Series B at $1.45B (backed by Amazon, GV, and AMD) to build world-simulation AI infrastructure, while DeepSeek V4 prices at $0.87 per million output tokens and GLM-5.2 ships an MIT-licensed 1M-context open-weights model.

title: The AI Brief — Vol. 02, Issue 25
summary: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5 (80.3% SWE-bench Pro, the highest public coding score ever) and then suspends global access within 72 hours after a US Commerce Department export-control directive — the first retroactive ban on a commercially released AI model. Also this week: Apple WWDC 2026 confirms Siri AI rebuilt with Google Gemini across 2.2B devices as Tim Cook announces his September retirement; OpenAI files a confidential S-1 targeting ~$1T IPO; and MiniMax 3 delivers frontier-class multimodal performance at $0.53 per million tokens.

title: The AI Brief — Vol. 02, Issue 24
summary: Microsoft launches 7 MAI models at Build 2026 — trained without OpenAI data — marking a direct pivot to self-sufficiency; Anthropic discloses Claude writes 80%+ of its own code and warns of recursive self-improvement risk; OpenAI targets a September IPO at $850B while Anthropic files its own S-1; and Google agrees to pay xAI $920M/month for compute, alongside Anthropic's existing $1.25B/month deal.

title: The AI Brief — Vol. 02, Issue 23
summary: OpenAI opens its IPO roadshow at a $1.75T valuation; Anthropic enters $1T term-sheet talks after its first operating profit; Tim Gowers verifies OpenAI's Erdos proof as a second model run tightens the unit-distance bound to n^1.05; and Apple previews third-party AI Extensions for iOS at WWDC.

title: The AI Brief — Vol. 02, Issue 22
summary: OpenAI's reasoning model autonomously disproves an 80-year geometry conjecture with a 125-page proof; Meta commits $145B to AI while cutting 8,000 jobs; Anthropic posts its first operating profit on $10.9B Q2 revenue; and a supply chain attack steals 3,800 GitHub repos in an 18-minute window.
